maltider.meta: The Cottage kitchen · All year round · Ten people
intro: A buffet lets everyone come down at their own pace: coffee first, bread next, and an egg once you are awake. Everything can be prepared the evening before.
With it, sourdough bread, cheese, butter, homemade jam and coffee from the espresso machine.
recept: Granola

Mix 500 g rolled oats, 150 g chopped nuts and seeds, 1 tsp salt and 1 tsp cinnamon. Warm 1 dl rapeseed oil and 1 dl honey and stir into the dry ingredients. Toast in the oven at 150 °C for 30–35 minutes, stirring twice. Let it cool before adding dried fruit.
Berry compote
Simmer 500 g frozen berries from the forest garden with 2 tbsp sugar for five minutes. Mix 1 tsp potato starch with a little cold water and stir it in. Serve lukewarm with soured milk and yoghurt.
Six-minute eggs
Put the eggs into boiling water and boil for exactly six minutes. Cool at once in cold water. The yolk is jammy and the white firm.

duk.Bord: The Cottage kitchen table, with the bread and the granola on the granite shelf behind.
duk.Duk: Pastel, pale yellow, with white linen napkins.
duk.Porslin: Figgjo as the base, Nittsjö bowls for berries and porridge.
duk.Glas: The water glasses and SEA for juice.
duk.Bestick: Wood and horn, with the Joinery’s knives in the butter.
duk.Ljus och grönt: A tea light in a glass and a jug of whatever is in flower.

maltider.meta: The Orangery · Spring to autumn · Twelve people
intro: Brunch is the weekend’s long breakfast, in the light through the old windows. It is best when it is allowed to take hours and someone fries pancakes in batches.
With it, sourdough bread, smoked salmon, cheese and a big bowl of berries.
recept: Ricotta pancakes

Stir together 500 g ricotta, 4 eggs, 2 tbsp sugar and the grated zest of a lemon. Fold in 1.5 dl plain flour mixed with 1 tsp baking powder. Fry small pancakes in butter, 2–3 minutes per side, and keep them warm in the oven at 100 °C. It makes about sixteen. Serve with fresh berries and jam.
Scrambled eggs with herbs
Whisk 12 eggs with 1 dl milk and salt. Cook slowly over a low heat in butter, stirring all the time. Take off the heat while the eggs are still a little glossy. Scatter over chopped chives and dill.
Lemon yoghurt
Stir 5 dl Greek yoghurt with the zest of a lemon, 2 tbsp honey and a pinch of salt.

duk.Bord: The long table, with the fruit from the citrus trees in a big bowl.
duk.Duk: White linen, with a pastel runner.
duk.Porslin: Bitz stoneware as the base, Figgjo for the pancakes.
duk.Glas: SEA for juice and the water glasses.
duk.Bestick: Old silver and the Joinery’s knives.
duk.Ljus och grönt: The sun is enough, but a tea light in a glass belongs. Flowers in a jug.

maltider.titel: Sandwiches and bagels in the studio
maltider.meta: The studio kitchen · All year round · Eight people
intro: Lunch with paint on your hands: bagels that can be eaten with one hand and fillings that can stand out all day.
recept: Bagels, eight

Dissolve 15 g fresh yeast in 2.5 dl lukewarm water. Add 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tsp salt and 500 g strong flour and knead for ten minutes into a firm dough. Leave to rise under a cloth for an hour. Divide into eight, roll into balls and press a hole in each. Rest for 20 minutes. Boil for 1 minute per side in water with 1 tbsp honey. Place on a tray and bake for 15–18 minutes at 220 °C.
Fillings
Gravlax with dill, red onion and capers. Egg salad with chives. Hummus with fried pepper and rocket. Cheese, apple and mustard. Lay everything out on large boards and let the guests build their own.

duk.Bord: The studio table, cleared and covered.
duk.Duk: Blue checked linen, which is allowed to get stained.
duk.Porslin: The Workshop tableware in Lime, with large olive-wood platters.
duk.Glas: The water glasses and jars of brewed tea.
duk.Ljus och grönt: A small candle and a bunch of herbs in a jar.

maltider.titel: Green platters – salads and a vegetarian lunch
maltider.meta: The garden tables · Early summer to late summer · Eight people · Vegetarian, easily made vegan
intro: Three salads that together make a meal. They are best when the garden gives more than anyone can eat.
With it, focaccia or sourdough bread and a piece of cheese.
recept: Tomato salad
Cut 1 kg tomatoes of different colours and sizes. Mix with 2 tbsp red wine vinegar, 4 tbsp olive oil, salt and a generous handful of basil. Leave for twenty minutes.
New potato salad
Boil 800 g new potatoes with dill. Mix while warm with 2 dl crème fraîche, 1 bunch chopped chives and 1 tbsp Dijon mustard. (Vegan version: oat yoghurt and oil.)
White beans with lemon
Rinse 3 tins of white beans. Toss with the zest and juice of a lemon, 4 tbsp olive oil, 1 chopped garlic clove and chopped parsley.

duk.Bord: The garden tables, pushed together under the apple trees.
duk.Duk: Checked linen or white linen.
duk.Porslin: Nittsjö and the Workshop tableware in Moss as the base, Turquoise for the small dishes.
duk.Glas: SEA and the water glasses, ideally with rosé.
duk.Ljus och grönt: Jars of nettles, camomile and red clover along the table.

maltider.dukmeta: Early summer to late summer · Under the fruit trees

maltider.meta: The Meadow · Summer · Six people
intro: The table setting you can carry with you: everything must pack into a basket and be eaten with the hands.
recept: Picnic frittata

Chop 1 onion and fry in oil. Mix with 300 g boiled, sliced potatoes and 150 g crumbled goat’s cheese in an ovenproof dish. Whisk 10 eggs with 1 dl milk, salt and chopped herbs and pour over. Bake at 200 °C for 20–25 minutes. Cut into squares and eat cold.
Sandwiches with herb butter
Stir 150 g softened butter with dill, chives and salt. Spread on sourdough bread and top with cucumber and cheese.
Elderflower lemonade
Boil 1 litre of water with 1 dl sugar. Add the zest and juice of two lemons and 10 elderflower heads. Leave to steep overnight, strain and dilute with cold water.

duk.Bord: None. A wool blanket in the grass, with a basket in the middle.
duk.Duk: A wool blanket, and white linen over the basket.
duk.Porslin: Enamel mugs and light plates from the Workshop tableware.
duk.Glas: Jars for the lemonade.
duk.Ljus och grönt: Meadow flowers in a jar. No candles – daylight is enough.

maltider.meta: The fire place · Late summer · Thirty people, day visit
intro: A big griddle pan, long ladles and a whole evening. Everything goes on the same surface, and the guests eat straight from the fire.
Serve with soured cream, chilli sauce and chopped parsley. Finish with thin pancakes on the griddle with jam.
recept: Muurikka potatoes

Boil 6 kg potatoes in their skins until almost done, cool and cut into wedges. Heat the muurikka over embers, add 1 dl oil and fry the potatoes in batches until golden. Salt, add plenty of butter and 2 kg sliced onion towards the end.
Vegetables and mushrooms
Fry 3 kg courgettes and peppers in thick slices, and 1.5 kg mushrooms without lids. Season with salt, thyme and garlic.
Sausages and halloumi
Grill 3 kg sausages and 2 kg sliced halloumi at the edges of the griddle.

duk.Bord: The plank table and two garden tables beside it.
duk.Duk: None. Bare wood.
duk.Porslin: Enamel and cast iron for the food, the Workshop tableware in Rust for the guests.
duk.Glas: The water glasses and Smoke grey.
duk.Bestick: Wood and horn, with wooden serving ware.
duk.Ljus och grönt: Lanterns on the table and in the trees, and the fire.

maltider.titel: Barbecue evening in the outdoor kitchen
maltider.meta: The outdoor kitchen · Late summer · Eight people
intro: The gas grill for fish and vegetables, the charcoal grill for meat. On a summer evening both are used at once.
recept: Grilled Arctic char or salmon
Rub a whole 1.5 kg fish with oil, salt and lemon slices. Fill with dill and thyme. Grill for 12–15 minutes per side over indirect heat, until the flesh comes away from the bones.
Charcoal-grilled rib-eye
Take 1.2 kg rib-eye out an hour in advance. Salt generously and grill for 3–4 minutes per side over hot charcoal. Rest for 10 minutes under foil and slice against the grain.
Vegetables and halloumi
Grill 2 sliced aubergines, 3 corn cobs and 400 g sliced halloumi. Drizzle with oil and lemon.
Herb sauce
Blend a cup of parsley, a cup of chives, 2 garlic cloves, the juice of a lemon, 1 dl olive oil and salt.

duk.Bord: The garden tables in front of the black granite.
duk.Duk: Rust and ochre, or just bare wood.
duk.Porslin: The Workshop tableware in Rust, with Nittsjö bowls for salads.
duk.Glas: Smoke grey and the water glasses.
duk.Ljus och grönt: The light strings over the outdoor kitchen and lanterns in the trees.

maltider.titel: Pizza evening at the wood-fired oven
maltider.meta: The outdoor kitchen · Summer · Twelve people
intro: The dough is made the day before. The oven is heated for an hour. The rest is play.
recept: Pizza dough, twelve balls

Dissolve 6 g dried yeast in 1.3 litres of lukewarm water. Mix in 2 kg strong flour and 50 g salt and knead until the dough comes away from the bowl. Rest for 30 minutes, divide into twelve balls of about 280 g and place in a sealed box. Keep in the fridge for 24 hours and take out two hours before baking.
Tomato sauce
Mix 2 tins of chopped tomatoes with salt, olive oil and a pinch of sugar. No cooking.
Toppings
Mozzarella, mushrooms, red onion, herbs from the garden, ham and rocket.
Baking
The oven should be 400–450 °C. Bake the pizza for 60–90 seconds, turning with the peel. Serve at once.

duk.Bord: The garden tables or the bistro table, near the oven.
duk.Duk: Checked linen.
duk.Porslin: The Workshop tableware in Lime and Figgjo.
duk.Glas: The water glasses and jars for lemonade.
duk.Bestick: The Joinery’s knives and wood and horn.
duk.Ljus och grönt: The light strings and a pot of basil on every table.

maltider.titel: Whole roast lamb by the fire
maltider.meta: The fire place · Autumn · Thirty to thirty-five people
intro: It is the whole day’s project. The fire is lit in the morning and the meat turned until it is time to eat.
recept: The lamb

A whole lamb of 18–20 kg (carcass weight). Rub with 400 g salt, rosemary, garlic, olive oil and lemon the evening before. Set on a spit over even embers, 90–120 cm above the fire. Turn regularly for six to eight hours. The meat must reach at least 70 °C in the thickest part. Rest under foil for 30 minutes before carving.
Accompaniments
Roast potatoes, grilled roots and a big bowl of yoghurt sauce with mint and garlic.
Respect
The fire is watched all the time. Water and a fire blanket must be close by. During a fire ban we roast in the outdoor kitchen instead.

duk.Bord: The plank table and the garden tables in a row.
duk.Duk: No cloth, but a runner in rust and ochre.
duk.Porslin: Enamel, cast iron and the Workshop tableware in Rust.
duk.Glas: Smoke grey and the water glasses.
duk.Bestick: Wood and horn, and large tongs.
duk.Ljus och grönt: Lanterns in the trees, candles in jars and the fire at the centre.

maltider.meta: The fire place · Autumn · Eight people
intro: Three Dutch ovens in the embers: bread, stew and pie. All you need is patience.
Serve everything in the pots.
recept: Bread

Mix 500 g strong flour, 1 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp dried yeast and 3.5 dl cold water. Leave to rise for 12–18 hours. Place in a preheated Dutch oven. Bake with the lid on for 30 minutes and without it for 15.
Root vegetable and lamb stew
Brown 1 kg lamb pieces and add 1 kg root vegetables, 2 onions, 5 garlic cloves, 4 dl stock, thyme and 1 tbsp tomato purée. Cook in the embers for 2 hours with coals on the lid.
Apple pie

Mix 6 sliced apples with cinnamon and sugar in a third Dutch oven. Crumble over 150 g butter, 2 dl rolled oats, 1 dl flour and 1 dl raw cane sugar. Coals underneath and on top. Ready after 40 minutes.

duk.Bord: The plank table beside the hearth.
duk.Duk: Rust and ochre, laid loosely over the planks.
duk.Porslin: Cast iron and enamel for the food, Bitz bowls for the pie.
duk.Glas: Glögg if it is cold, otherwise the water glasses.
duk.Bestick: Wood and horn, and wooden serving ware.
duk.Ljus och grönt: Lanterns, jars with candles and, in November, spruce sprigs.

maltider.titel: Crayfish party under the fruit trees
maltider.meta: The garden tables · Late summer · Twelve people
intro: A playful table setting that can take dirty hands and lasts the whole evening.
With it, potatoes in dill sauce, bread, cheese and snaps.
recept: Crayfish

Allow fifteen crayfish per person. Bring 5 litres of water to the boil with 6 dl salt, 1 dl sugar, 3 bunches of crown dill, 1 tbsp caraway and a bottle of pale beer. Add the crayfish and boil for three minutes after it returns to the boil. Leave the crayfish in the brine in the fridge overnight.
Västerbotten cheese pie

Mix 150 g butter, 3 dl plain flour and 1 tbsp cold water into a shortcrust and line a tin. Blind-bake at 200 °C for 10 minutes. Whisk 3 eggs with 3 dl soured cream, add 3 dl grated Västerbotten cheese, black pepper and 1 chopped red onion. Bake for 25–30 minutes.

duk.Bord: The garden tables in a long row.
duk.Duk: White linen with paper napkins – it is a crayfish party.
duk.Porslin: Vienna and Figgjo, and large platters for the crayfish.
duk.Glas: Snaps and the water glasses.
duk.Ljus och grönt: Lanterns and paper moons in the trees, dill in heaps along the table.

maltider.dukmeta: Late summer · Under the fruit trees

maltider.titel: Soup and bread in the Cottage
maltider.meta: The Cottage kitchen · Autumn · Eight people · Vegetarian
intro: Pumpkin soup made in a single pot, and a bread that makes itself.
recept: Roast pumpkin soup

Peel and dice 1 kg pumpkin, 3 carrots and 1 onion. Roast with oil, salt and 3 garlic cloves at 220 °C for 30 minutes. Blend with 1 litre of vegetable stock and 1 tbsp grated fresh ginger. Add 1 dl cream (or oat cream) and season with lemon. Top with toasted pumpkin seeds and parsley.
Buttermilk bread

Mix 500 g plain flour, 1 tsp bicarbonate of soda and 1.5 tsp salt. Stir in 4 dl buttermilk to a sticky dough. Shape into a round on a tray, cut a cross in the top and bake at 200 °C for 40 minutes. The bread is ready when it sounds hollow when tapped.

duk.Bord: The Cottage kitchen table, with the soup on the table in its pot.
duk.Duk: Rust and ochre, or just bare wood.
duk.Porslin: Nittsjö bowls and the Workshop tableware in Moss.
duk.Glas: The water glasses.
duk.Bestick: Wood and horn, and the Joinery’s knives.
duk.Ljus och grönt: The Tiffany lamp is lit, and candles in brass candlesticks at different heights.

maltider.meta: The tipi · Autumn · Eight people
intro: A circle round a low table. The food comes from the fire and is eaten with the hands.
recept: Venison stew with juniper

Brown 1.2 kg diced venison in butter, add two sliced onions, two carrots, 5 crushed juniper berries and 3 dl red wine. Add 5 dl water and 1 tbsp venison stock. Cook covered over the fire for two hours. Finish with 1 tbsp blackcurrant jelly and salt. (Mushroom stew with chanterelles for vegetarians.)
Flatbread over the fire
Mix 6 dl plain flour, 2 dl water, 1 tsp salt and 1 tbsp oil. Roll out into thin rounds and bake directly on a hot iron griddle, a minute per side.

duk.Bord: The low table, with cushions and a wool blanket all round.
duk.Duk: Sheepskins on the floor, an embroidered runner on the table.
duk.Porslin: Bitz and the Workshop tableware in Rust.
duk.Glas: Glögg if it is cold, otherwise the water glasses.
duk.Ljus och grönt: Lanterns on the floor and candles in jars.

maltider.meta: The sauna · All year round · Eight people
intro: The simplest of all – and the one that tastes best. The body is warm and hungry; the food should be cold and salty.
recept: Gravlax

Mix 3 tbsp coarse salt, 3 tbsp sugar and 1 tbsp crushed white pepper. Rub 1 kg salmon fillet with the mixture, lay dill on top and cover with foil. Put in the fridge with a weight on top for two days, turning once. Slice thinly.
Mustard sauce
Stir together 2 tbsp sweet mustard, 1 tbsp Dijon mustard, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp vinegar and 1 dl oil, and stir in chopped dill.
Rye bread and pickled cucumber
Slice the rye bread thinly and serve with butter and pickled cucumber from the garden. Cold drinks in glass bottles: apple juice, beer and sparkling water.

duk.Bord: A low table on the deck, or just planks on trestles.
duk.Duk: Towels instead of cloths, and a runner in Soft blue.
duk.Porslin: The Workshop tableware in Lime and wooden trays.
duk.Glas: The water glasses and glass bottles of drinks.
duk.Ljus och grönt: Lanterns in the blue hour.

maltider.meta: The Cottage kitchen · Winter · Six people
intro: Fondue is perhaps the cosiest meal of all – you share a pot, and nobody is in a hurry.
recept: Cheese fondue

Rub a fondue pot with a garlic clove. Warm 3 dl dry white wine. Stir in 400 g grated Gruyère and 400 g grated Emmental in batches, stirring in figures of eight until the cheese has melted. Mix 1 tbsp cornflour with 1 tbsp kirsch and stir it in. Season with nutmeg and pepper.
For dipping
Cubes of sourdough bread, boiled new potatoes, pickled cucumber, silverskin onions and pear.

duk.Bord: The Cottage kitchen table, scaled down to six.
duk.Duk: Red checked linen.
duk.Porslin: Figgjo and Nittsjö bowls.
duk.Glas: SEA for the wine and the water glasses.
duk.Bestick: Fondue forks, old silver and wood and horn.
duk.Ljus och grönt: Brass candlesticks, and a candle on each side of the pot.

maltider.meta: The Cottage or the orangery · Spring · Ten people
intro: The first festival of spring is laid light and simple, with the spring light that is finally coming back.
recept: Nettle soup

Pick 2 litres of nettles (with gloves) and blanch them quickly. Soften 1 onion in butter, add 2 sliced potatoes and 1 litre of stock and simmer until the potatoes are soft. Add the nettles, blend and season with cream and lemon. Serve with halved boiled eggs.
Roast lamb with garlic
Pierce a 2 kg leg of lamb and fill the holes with garlic and rosemary. Rub with salt and oil. Roast at 160 °C to 68 °C in the centre, about two hours. Rest for 20 minutes.
Smoked salmon and eggs
Smoked salmon, fresh eggs and rye bread, as always.

duk.Bord: The Cottage kitchen table, or the long table in the orangery.
duk.Duk: Pastel in yellow or pale green.
duk.Porslin: Celadon as the base and Inger for the coffee.
duk.Glas: SEA and the water glasses.
duk.Ljus och grönt: Birch twigs with feathers, painted eggs and daffodils in ceramic jugs.

maltider.dukmeta: Spring · The Cottage or the Orangery

maltider.meta: The Meadow · Early summer · Sixteen to twenty people, day visit
intro: The Midsummer table should feel as if it has grown up out of the meadow.
recept: New potatoes with dill
Boil 2 kg new potatoes with a large sprig of dill and salt. Serve with butter and chopped dill.
Herring in three flavours
Buy good herring and marinate it in three dressings: mustard, dill, and chives with soured cream. Serve with crispbread and Västerbotten cheese.
Midsummer cake

Whisk 4 eggs with 2 dl sugar until pale and fluffy. Fold in 1 dl plain flour, 1 dl potato starch and 1 tsp baking powder. Bake at 175 °C for 30 minutes. Split into three layers, fill with 6 dl whipped cream and 1 kg strawberries, and cover with more cream.

duk.Bord: The garden tables in a long row in the meadow.
duk.Duk: White linen, straight on the grass and the table.
duk.Porslin: Mixed – Figgjo, Celadon and Coq.
duk.Glas: Snaps and the water glasses.
duk.Bestick: Wood and horn and old silver, mixed.
duk.Ljus och grönt: Meadow flowers in jars, flower crowns and birch leaves along the table.

maltider.meta: The Orangery, or the garden tables · Autumn · Sixteen people
intro: The harvest festival table is a thank-you to the garden.
With it, apple juice in glass jugs.
recept: Roast root vegetables
Cut 2 kg root vegetables into wedges and mix with oil, salt, 2 tbsp honey and fresh thyme. Roast at 225 °C for 30–40 minutes.
Mushroom soup
Fry 500 g wild mushrooms with onion in butter. Add 1.2 litres of vegetable stock and 2 dl cream. Simmer for 10 minutes and blend coarsely.
Apple crumble cake
Slice 8 apples into a dish. Rub 150 g butter with 2 dl rolled oats, 1 dl flour and 1 dl raw cane sugar and scatter over. Bake at 200 °C for 25–30 minutes. Serve with vanilla custard.

duk.Bord: The long table, or the garden tables under the roof.
duk.Duk: Rust and ochre.
duk.Porslin: Bitz and the Workshop tableware in Rust.
duk.Glas: Hovmantorp for sparkling apple juice, otherwise the water glasses.
duk.Ljus och grönt: Apples, pumpkins and squashes along the table, sheaves of grain and candles.

maltider.meta: The Cottage · December · Twelve people
intro: One of the simplest and loveliest table settings of the year, in the dark morning.
With it, gingersnaps and coffee.
recept: Saffron buns, twenty-four

Melt 150 g butter and add 5 dl milk. Warm to blood heat and dissolve 50 g fresh yeast in it. Add 1 g saffron, 1.5 dl sugar and 1 tsp salt. Knead in about 14 dl plain flour (around 800 g). Leave to rise for 45 minutes. Divide into 24 pieces, roll out and shape into an S. Brush with beaten egg and press in raisins. Bake at 225 °C for 8–10 minutes.
Alcohol-free glögg
Simmer 1 litre of blackcurrant juice with 1 cinnamon stick, 5 cloves, 3 cardamom pods and the peel of an orange for 15 minutes. Serve with almonds and raisins.

duk.Bord: The Cottage kitchen table, joined to a garden table.
duk.Duk: White linen.
duk.Porslin: Inger for the coffee, Coq for the buns.
duk.Glas: Glögg.
duk.Ljus och grönt: Lingonberry sprigs and candles in brass candlesticks in the dark morning.

maltider.meta: The Cottage or the orangery · Christmas · Sixteen people
intro: The Christmas table is the table setting of tradition – the one everyone knows how it should look.
With it, herring, saffron bread, sausages, beetroot salad and rice pudding.
recept: Christmas ham

Put a 4 kg lightly salted ham in water and simmer slowly until it reaches 70 °C in the centre, about three hours. Remove the rind, brush with mustard and sprinkle with breadcrumbs. Brown for 10 minutes at 225 °C.
Jansson’s temptation

Cut 1 kg potatoes into matchsticks and slice 2 onions thinly. Layer in a dish with 2 tins of sprats (about 250 g) and pour over 3 dl cream. Sprinkle with breadcrumbs and flakes of butter and bake at 200 °C for 45 minutes.
Red cabbage
Slice half a kilo of red cabbage and simmer with 1 apple, 2 tbsp butter, 1 dl red wine vinegar and 1 dl sugar for 45 minutes.

duk.Bord: The long table, or the Cottage kitchen table with a garden table beside it.
duk.Duk: Red and white.
duk.Porslin: Variation or Classic Rose.
duk.Glas: Blåstjälken and Hovmantorp.
duk.Ljus och grönt: Brass candlesticks, spruce sprigs and the candelabras.

maltider.dukmeta: Christmas · The Cottage or the Orangery

maltider.meta: The Orangery · Winter · Twelve people
intro: The New Year table setting may well be the most elegant of the whole year.
recept: Toast Skagen
Mix 600 g peeled prawns with 2 dl crème fraîche, 1 dl mayonnaise, 1 bunch dill, the juice of a lemon and 1 chopped red onion. Toast the bread. Top with 3 tbsp vendace roe.
Oysters
Allow 3 per person. Serve with lemon and red wine vinegar with finely chopped shallot.
Chocolate mousse
Melt 200 g dark chocolate. Stir in 4 egg yolks, whisk the whites to stiff peaks and the cream separately. Fold together gently, divide into glasses and leave to set for three hours.

duk.Bord: The long table.
duk.Duk: Dark green velvet as a runner over white linen.
duk.Porslin: Classic Rose and Variation.
duk.Glas: Blåstjälken, Hovmantorp for the champagne.
duk.Ljus och grönt: The candelabras and a profusion of candles. A little confetti.

maltider.meta: The Cottage kitchen · Autumn · Eight people
intro: Five small dishes instead of three large ones. Everything can be prepared in advance, and the last thing cooked is the venison.
recept: 1. Blinis with vendace roe

Stir together 3 dl lukewarm milk, 1.5 dl plain flour, 1.5 dl buckwheat flour, 1 egg yolk, 12 g fresh yeast and 1 tsp salt. Leave to rise for an hour. Whisk the egg white and fold it in. Fry small pancakes in butter. Top with crème fraîche, vendace roe and dill.
2. Beetroot carpaccio
Roast 4 beetroots in foil at 200 °C for an hour, peel and slice thinly. Lay on a plate with crumbled goat’s cheese (150 g), toasted hazelnuts, olive oil and a few drops of balsamic vinegar.
3. Pan-fried Arctic char
Salt 8 fillets of 120 g each. Fry skin side down for 3 minutes until the skin is crisp and turn briefly. Sauce: reduce 2 dl white wine with 1 chopped shallot, add 2 dl cream, lemon and dill.
4. Fillet of venison with celeriac purée

Season 1 kg venison fillet with salt and pepper, brown in butter on all sides and roast at 120 °C to 56–58 °C in the centre. Rest for 10 minutes. Purée: simmer 800 g celeriac in 3 dl milk and 1 dl water, blend with 50 g butter. Jus: reduce 3 dl venison stock with 2 dl red wine by half and stir in 1 tbsp blackcurrant jelly.
5. Panna cotta with sea buckthorn

Soak 3 gelatine leaves. Warm 5 dl cream, 2 dl milk and 1 dl sugar with vanilla seeds. Dissolve the gelatine in the warm mixture. Divide into glasses and leave to set for four hours. Serve with sea buckthorn jam.

duk.Bord: The Cottage kitchen table, laid for eight with plenty of room.
duk.Duk: White linen, ironed, with napkins in the same tone.
duk.Porslin: Classic Rose for the starters, Celadon for the fish, Variation for the venison and Inger for the dessert.
duk.Glas: Hovmantorp for the first glass, Blåstjälken for the wine and the water glasses.
duk.Bestick: Old silver, laid from the outside in, in order.
duk.Ljus och grönt: The candelabras, and a single branch in a vase.

maltider.titel: Romantic tea party in the garden
maltider.meta: The Garden · Summer · Two to four people
intro: A tea party is a table setting of its own: slow, small and full of little things. Time is all you need.
Tea: Earl Grey or lime blossom tea from the garden.
recept: Scones, twelve

Mix 500 g plain flour, 1 tbsp baking powder, 75 g sugar and 1 tsp salt. Grate in 125 g cold butter. Stir in 1 egg and 2 dl milk to a soft dough. Roll out and cut. Bake at 220 °C for 12–15 minutes. Serve warm with whipped cream and jam.
Cucumber sandwiches
Cut thin slices of white bread into triangles, spread with butter and lay on thinly sliced cucumber. Salt lightly.
Strawberries with rose water
Mix 400 g strawberries with 1 tbsp sugar and 1 tsp rose water.

duk.Bord: The bistro table, a small round one with two chairs.
duk.Duk: Lace over white linen.
duk.Porslin: Inger in bone china, and tiered stands with scones and sandwiches.
duk.Glas: The water glasses.
duk.Bestick: Old silver, with a silver teapot.
duk.Ljus och grönt: Roses in a jug and candles in glass.

maltider.titel: Dinner for two under the oak
maltider.meta: Under the oak · Summer evening · Two people
intro: Vreta is also a place for two. The table setting is small, simple and carries itself.
recept: Tomato and burrata
Cut 300 g tomatoes, lay on a platter with 1 burrata, drizzle with oil, salt and tear over basil.
Pan-fried Arctic char with brown butter

Fry 2 Arctic char fillets of 150 g each in butter, skin side first. Brown butter: brown 50 g butter until it smells nutty, add the juice of half a lemon and 1 tbsp capers. Serve with 400 g new potatoes.
Strawberries with mascarpone
Mix 100 g mascarpone with 1 tbsp icing sugar and serve with 250 g strawberries.

duk.Bord: A small table under the oak, with two chairs turned towards the garden.
duk.Duk: White linen.

maltider.titel: Winter tea party in the orangery
maltider.meta: The Orangery · Winter · Eight people
intro: When there is snow outside and lemons in the window.
recept: Lemon cake

Cream 150 g butter with 2 dl sugar until pale. Add 3 eggs one at a time. Fold in 2.5 dl plain flour, 1 tsp baking powder, the zest of two lemons and the juice of one. Bake at 175 °C for 40–45 minutes. Icing: stir 2 dl icing sugar with lemon juice.
Smoked salmon sandwiches
Rye bread, cream cheese, smoked salmon and dill.
Clementines and tea
Earl Grey, jasmine and lime blossom tea in large pots.

duk.Bord: The long table, laid at one end near the citrus trees.
duk.Duk: Lace over dark green velvet.
duk.Porslin: Inger and Celadon.
duk.Glas: Glögg for a hot drink, the water glasses.
duk.Ljus och grönt: The candelabras, and lemons and spruce sprigs in bowls.

maltider.meta: The outdoor kitchen · All year round · Ten people · Vegetarian
intro: Many small bowls and bread for dipping. Mezze is a meal to share.
With it, flatbread, pomegranate and mint tea.
recept: Hummus
Blend 400 g cooked chickpeas with 1.5 dl tahini, the juice of 2 lemons, 2 garlic cloves, 1 tsp salt and 1 dl iced water. Blend for a long time. Drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle with paprika.
Baba ganoush
Roast 3 whole aubergines at 220 °C for 45 minutes. Scrape out the flesh and mix with 1 dl tahini, the juice of a lemon, 1 crushed garlic clove and salt.
Tabbouleh
Soak 1.5 dl fine bulgur in 1 dl hot water for 15 minutes. Mix with 3 bunches chopped parsley, 1 bunch mint, 4 chopped tomatoes, the juice of 2 lemons, 1 dl olive oil and salt.

maltider.meta: Under the pergola · Summer · Eight people · Vegetarian
intro: A lunch that may take the whole afternoon.
recept: Focaccia

Mix 500 g strong flour, 4 dl cold water, 10 g salt and 3 g dried yeast. Leave to rest in the fridge for 12 hours. Put in an oiled tray, press holes with your fingers and drizzle with olive oil and sea salt. Bake at 230 °C for 20–25 minutes.
Tomatoes with burrata
Cut 1 kg tomatoes into pieces, mix with salt and olive oil and lay on a platter with 4 burrata. Scatter with basil.
Peaches in bubbles
Slice 8 ripe peaches, sprinkle with 2 tbsp sugar and pour over a bottle of cold, dry sparkling wine. Scatter with mint.

duk.Bord: The garden tables in a long row under the pergola.

maltider.meta: The outdoor kitchen · Late summer · Ten people
intro: North Africa in a Swedish garden, under the patterned Algerian ceiling panels.
With it, Moroccan mint tea.
recept: Lamb tagine with apricots

Brown 1.5 kg lamb pieces with 2 chopped onions, 1 tsp ginger, 1 tsp cinnamon, 1 tsp turmeric and 3 garlic cloves. Add 5 dl water, a pinch of saffron and 200 g dried apricots. Simmer covered for two hours. Top with toasted almonds.
Couscous
Pour 5 dl hot stock over 5 dl couscous. Leave to swell under a lid for five minutes. Fork through with 2 tbsp butter.
Carrot salad
Grate 6 carrots and mix with the juice of a lemon, 1 tsp cumin, oil and chopped coriander.

duk.Duk: An embroidered runner over rust and ochre.

maltider.meta: The Orangery, or the outdoor kitchen · Festive · Ten people · Vegetarian
intro: Everything is served at once on a platter with many small bowls.
With it, rice, chutney and pickled onions.
recept: Dal

Rinse 5 dl red lentils. Fry 1 chopped onion, 3 garlic cloves and 1 tbsp grated ginger in 2 tbsp oil. Add 1 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp cumin and 2 tomatoes. Add the lentils and 1.2 litres of water. Simmer for 20 minutes. Salt and season with lemon.
Raita
Mix 5 dl yoghurt with a grated cucumber, 1 tsp toasted cumin and salt.
Chapati, ten
Mix 300 g wholemeal flour, 1.8 dl water, 1 tsp salt and 1 tbsp oil. Rest for 30 minutes, roll thinly and cook in a dry, hot pan.

duk.Porslin: Brass platters and copper bowls as thali, Turquoise for rice and chutney.

maltider.titel: Japanese dinner and tea in the studio
maltider.meta: The studio kitchen · Autumn · Six people
intro: The Japanese plates from the collection get to show what they can do.
Finish with tea: whisk matcha in the tea bowls, in silence.
recept: Miso soup
Warm 1.2 litres of dashi (or water with 10 g kombu), stir in 3 tbsp miso, add 200 g diced tofu and 1 tbsp wakame. Scatter with spring onion. Do not boil once the miso is in.
Teriyaki salmon
Mix 1 dl soy sauce, 1 dl mirin, 2 tbsp sugar and 1 tbsp grated ginger. Fry 800 g salmon pieces, pour over the sauce and let it reduce.
Onigiri
Cook 4 dl Japanese rice. Shape into triangles with wet hands, press salted salmon into the middle and wrap in nori.
Pickled cucumber
Slice 2 cucumbers and mix with 1 dl rice vinegar, 1 tbsp sugar and 1 tsp salt.

kok: The everyday kitchen. Newly renovated since last autumn – green, warm and full of light and brass.
The kitchen for feasts. Sixty square metres with the kitchen from Hornsgatan, cartwheel chandeliers and artichoke lamps.
The summer kitchen. Syrian limestone, Algerian ceiling panels, grills, a wood-fired ceramic oven and the bar in Neo-Renaissance cupboards.
The working day’s kitchen. A simple kitchen from Djursholm in the artists’ studio.
kok_p: Four kitchens on one plot may sound a lot. But they serve different purposes, and they are used at different times and for different kinds of meeting. The Cottage kitchen is the everyday one: breakfast, dinner for family and friends, evenings by the granite shelf. The orangery kitchen is for feasts and courses: room for many, in the middle of the citrus trees. The outdoor kitchen belongs to summer and fire. The studio kitchen is for the working day – the simple one, where you top up your coffee and eat a sandwich between brushstrokes.
Besides the kitchens there are the fire places: grill places for the muurikka, spits and large pots out on the plot. They are in a way the fifth kitchen – the oldest of them all.
principer: Surfaces, utensils and vessels that are enough when twenty come instead of four.
Room for several at the counter. Nobody should have to stand alone at the stove.
What is in the garden and close by comes first. What does not grow here is used with pleasure.
Kitchens, china and utensils with a history – that will last for generations more.
The table setting is part of the food.
How a meal looks and feels matters as much as how it tastes.
lager_p: Every table setting at Vreta is built in the same order, whether it is a picnic blanket or a Christmas table for sixteen. Whoever knows the order can lay anything with anything.
lager: Where we sit and how many we are decides everything else.
The foundation. It gives the table colour, tone and softness.
What carries the food. This is where the big choices are made.
What the guest holds throughout the meal – and what catches the light.
Last, and most important. The candles are lit before the guests arrive.
loftet: It is easy to see the table setting as a detail – something done quickly before the food is ready. But whoever has sat at a beautifully laid table knows that it changes the whole meal. Guests sit down more slowly, conversation grows warmer and the food tastes better. A laid table says: we have been waiting for you, and we have done this for your sake.

At Vreta the table setting is therefore of the highest importance. It is part of the hosting, part of the art and part of the reuse. Almost everything on the tables has had a life before: china from house clearances and auctions, glass from the Kingdom of Crystal, linen from the sewing room, cutlery from flea markets and tables from the joinery. This chapter is the collection – the inventory from which the cookbook’s thirty meals are laid. Every table setting there refers to the names here.
omaka: Choose one tone – celadon green, moss, rust – and let everything else be neutral.
Only stoneware, only wood, only glass and linen. The material ties together what does not match.
Three kinds of plate, three kinds of glass, three heights of candle. More becomes disorder.
A long platter, a pot, a branch. It gives the table a centre.
Something with a history. Guests always ask.
sasong: Nettles, ramsons, rhubarb, asparagus and the first salads. Eggs from the hens.
Strawberries, new potatoes, dill and herring. The food of Midsummer.
Tomatoes, beans, courgettes, berries and crayfish. The high season of the grill.
Apples, juice, mushrooms, roots, game and lamb. The feasts of the harvest.
What is stored, preserved and fermented. Stew, bread and the Christmas table.
porslin: The white china is the resting pulse of the table setting. It lets the linen and the flowers show.

Besides the plates there is what the food is stirred, carried and served in: large ceramic platters, wooden trays from the joinery, olive-wood boards, enamelled pots straight from the fire, cast-iron pans, brass platters and copper bowls. They are not china, but they are just as much table setting. A muurikka or a pot from the embers on the table says more than any flower.
kokbok_cards: Unless otherwise stated the recipes are for eight people. The fire recipes are for more, as stated.
Every meal has a place at Vreta.
When the meal is at its best. Feel free to swap vegetables for whatever the garden gives.
Every meal ends with a table setting. All the names are in the chapter What carries the table.
Always ask the guests. Meals that are vegetarian or easily made vegan are marked in the text.
porslin_p: The china at Vreta is a collection of finds and our own work. It rests on a dozen or so services and series, and each table setting chooses one of them as the lead and lets a couple of others keep it company. Together they are enough for a long table for more than fifty guests – and for laying entirely different tables on the same evening.
